item.title: Why do so many legacy brands implode when trying to attract new customers?
item.description: There is a type of business story that has become nearly cliché: A legacy brand is facing stagnating growth. Loyal customers are aging out, and new customers aren’t taking their place. So the brand reinvents itself to pull in a younger segment of the market, often by borrowing ideas from cooler competitors to seem more “on-trend.” But instead of younger and cooler, the rebrand comes off as insincere, stilted, or cringey.
